title: Board pack Q3
text: Quarterly decisions are assessed against the charter and approved risk appetite. The board reviewed the 2027 forecast, supplier exposure, capital allocation and executive incentive proposals.
summary: The Q3 pack records board decisions on forecast, supplier exposure and incentives against the charter and risk appetite.

insights.text: Decisions reference the charter’s risk appetite, while supplier exposure and incentive evidence remain open for follow-up.
Forecast movements affect the proposed capital and incentive decisions.

title: Strategy note
text: The three-year plan prioritizes resilient growth, disciplined market entry and delivery of the customer platform. Quarterly milestones are reviewed by the executive team.
summary: Sets strategic priorities and the quarterly delivery review.

insights.text: Market entry depends on staged delivery milestones and named executive ownership.

title: Charter
text: The board sets purpose, strategic direction and risk appetite, and oversees management. Executives own delivery and maintain controls; the board reviews performance and material risks.
summary: Defines the board mandate, risk appetite and executive accountability.

insights.text: The board sets appetite; executives own delivery and controls.

title: Policy v4
text: Incentive payments require documented evidence that delivery targets were met and a second-person review before approval. Exceptions are reported to the remuneration committee.
summary: Sets evidence and review requirements for incentive payments and exceptions.

insights.text: A second-person check must document that incentive targets were met.

title: Controls memo
text: Control owners must retain evidence of review, record exceptions and escalate overdue actions. Finance checks incentive calculations against approved targets before payment.
summary: Assigns evidence retention, exception escalation and incentive calculation checks.

insights.text: Finance owns the documented target check before incentive payment.
Overdue control actions are escalated and retained in the evidence log.

title: Minutes · Sep
text: The committee discussed proposed executive incentives and asked for confirmation that delivery targets had been met. The evidence check was assigned to Finance for return at the next meeting.
summary: Records discussion of executive incentives and a follow-up evidence check.

insights.text: Finance was asked to provide target evidence before the proposed payment proceeds.

title: Forecast 2027
text: The base case includes planned platform investment, supplier continuity costs and forecast incentive expense. Liquidity remains within the board threshold in the base case but narrows under the downside scenario.
summary: Projects 2027 operating costs, investment and liquidity under base and downside cases.

insights.text: Downside liquidity headroom is narrower than the base case and depends on cost timing.

title: Training log
text: Completion is recorded for annual policy training. Several control-owner modules remain overdue; managers have been asked to confirm completion dates.
summary: Tracks policy training completion and overdue control-owner modules.

insights.text: Overdue control-owner training may delay consistent evidence handling.

title: Risk register
text: The register records supplier service interruption, cyber resilience and liquidity stress. Recovery plans for two critical suppliers have not been tested; mitigation owners and review dates are listed.
summary: Records key operational exposures, mitigation owners and review dates.

insights.text: Two critical supplier recovery plans remain untested.
Mitigation actions have owners but several review dates are due.

title: Audit plan
text: The annual plan includes supplier recovery testing, policy compliance sampling and review of control evidence. Testing will assess whether recovery time assumptions are supported by exercises.
summary: Schedules assurance work on supplier recovery, policy compliance and control evidence.

insights.text: Supplier recovery testing is planned, with evidence against recovery assumptions.

title: Supplier review
text: Critical suppliers provided recovery plans, but no recent exercise has tested them. Contract reviews identify service dependencies; owners are confirming recovery evidence and escalation contacts.
summary: Reviews critical supplier dependencies and identifies untested recovery plans.

insights.text: Recovery plans exist but have not been tested for critical suppliers.

title: Treasury update
text: Cash forecasts remain within minimum liquidity thresholds in the base case. A delayed customer receipt or accelerated supplier payment would reduce headroom; facilities remain available subject to covenants.
summary: Summarizes liquidity headroom, cash timing sensitivities and facility covenants.

insights.text: Cash timing sensitivity reduces headroom before the minimum threshold is reached.

title: Insurance schedule
text: The schedule lists interruption coverage, limits, deductibles and exclusions by policy. Recovery costs are subject to waiting periods and evidence of insured loss.
summary: Lists interruption coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions and evidence conditions.

insights.text: Interruption costs are subject to limits, waiting periods and proof of insured loss.

title: Board risk report
text: Two critical suppliers remain outside the board’s recovery expectations. The report summarizes untested plans, risk-register actions, insurance limits and the forecast cost of service interruption. Nobody clearly owns the risk for the new market launch.
summary: The Q3 risk report to the board. Two gaps stand out: supplier recovery plans that were never tested, and no clear owner for the new market launch risk.

insights.text: Two critical suppliers have no tested recovery plan.
Nobody clearly owns the risk for the new market launch.

title: Exec pay review
text: The committee reviewed proposed incentive payments and noted that delivery target evidence must be confirmed before payment. The follow-up check is assigned to Finance.
summary: Records proposed executive incentives and the outstanding target evidence check.

insights.text: The file does not include evidence that the proposed delivery targets were met.

title: Draft charter
text: The board sets risk appetite and strategic direction; executives own risk decisions and document accountability. This draft has not yet been connected to the approved charter.
summary: Draft language on risk ownership and board appetite, awaiting review.

insights.text: The draft assigns risk ownership to executives, matching the approved charter language.

title: Employment contracts
summary: Not in the vault.

title: Liquidity review
text: Liquidity headroom is sensitive to delayed receipts and supplier payment timing. The downside case approaches the board threshold; treasury will update the forecast after collections are confirmed.
summary: Reviews downside liquidity headroom and timing sensitivities.

insights.text: Downside headroom approaches the board threshold if receipts are delayed.

title: FY26 programme report · Sep
text: Overall programme status is green. The programme remains within its approved envelope: AED 29.8m of the approved AED 48m has been committed to date (62%), in line with the phasing agreed by the board in March. Milestone M3, go-live of the consolidated ledger in Q1 FY27, is on track. No material risks to the date have been identified by the programme office. Training for regional finance teams begins in November, with a readiness review scheduled for the December board. The intercompany and fixed-asset workstreams have no named owner.
summary: The September board report on the finance transformation. It reports the programme green and go-live milestone M3 on track for Q1 FY27, with spend at 62% of the approved AED 48m.

insights.text: Go-live milestone M3 is reported as on track.
Spend stands at 62% of the approved AED 48m budget.
Training for regional finance teams begins in November, ahead of the December readiness review.
Two workstreams report no named owner.

title: Risk register update · R-22
text: R-22, go-live of the consolidated ledger (milestone M3, Q1 FY27), is rated high. Four open risks sit against the same milestone: R-18 migrated balances do not yet reconcile within tolerance; R-19 regional finance training is not yet scheduled; R-20 the intercompany and fixed-asset workstreams have no named owner; R-21 bank payment file testing is incomplete. The board's risk appetite statement (§3) sets a low appetite for finance-system change: no core financial system goes live with an open high-rated risk. The mitigation owner for R-22 is the Programme Director; next review 30 November 2026.
summary: Group risk register update of 18 September. It rates the Q1 ledger go-live (R-22) high, with four open risks against milestone M3.

insights.text: The Q1 go-live (M3) is rated high risk, with four open risks against the same milestone.
Going live with an open high-rated risk falls outside the board's stated appetite for finance-system change.
Two workstreams have no named owner.

title: Cutover readiness checklist
text: Cutover readiness at 6 November: 23 of 31 go-live criteria met. Five open criteria are rated critical: migration reconciliation within the 0.5% tolerance (failed at rehearsal 2), regional training completion of at least 90% (not started), named owners for the intercompany and fixed-asset workstreams (open), bank payment file testing (in progress) and segregation-of-duties mapping (in progress). Cutover is planned for the weekend of 6–7 February 2027. Rollback to the legacy ledger stays available for 60 days after cutover. Vendor support and exit terms are not a checklist criterion.
summary: Go-live criteria for the consolidated ledger, tracked weekly. 23 of 31 are met; five critical criteria remain open three months before cutover.

insights.text: 23 of 31 go-live criteria are met; five open criteria are rated critical.
Rollback to the legacy ledger stays available for 60 days after cutover.
Vendor support and exit terms are not a checklist criterion.

title: Ledger training plan
text: 140 finance users across five regional teams must complete ledger training and pass a sandbox assessment before they receive access at cutover. Sessions are pencilled from 16 November to 18 December 2026; the trainer contract is unsigned and no regional date is confirmed. Trained to date: 0 of 140. The go-live gate requires 90% (126 users). The year-end close freezes training from 4 to 22 January 2027, so sessions that slip past December leave two weeks before the 6–7 February cutover. Any weekend sessions during the close depend on what the employment contracts allow.
summary: Plans ledger training for 140 regional finance users. No date is confirmed, nobody is trained yet, and the January close leaves little room if sessions slip.

insights.text: No regional training date is confirmed; sessions are pencilled from 16 November to 18 December.
Users without training receive no ledger access at cutover.
Sessions that slip past December leave two weeks of training before cutover.

title: Programme budget and slip cost
text: The approved programme envelope is AED 48m, of which AED 29.8m (62%) is committed. Contingency of AED 2.4m (5%) is undrawn. A one-quarter slip of go-live adds about AED 2.1m: AED 0.9m for parallel running of the legacy ledger, AED 0.8m for extended contractor cover and AED 0.4m for an extra migration rehearsal and retraining. That fits inside contingency with AED 0.3m to spare. The estimate excludes any CoreSys support fees after 31 March 2027, which depend on contract terms Finance has not seen.
summary: Tracks the AED 48m programme envelope and costs a one-quarter go-live slip at about AED 2.1m, inside contingency but before vendor fees.

insights.text: A one-quarter slip adds about AED 2.1m, inside the AED 2.4m contingency.
The slip estimate excludes CoreSys support fees after 31 March 2027.

title: Migration rehearsal 2 results
text: Rehearsal 2 (24–26 October) loaded 41,200 open items into the new ledger. 1,180 items (2.9%) failed reconciliation, against a go-live tolerance of 0.5%; rehearsal 1 in August failed 4.6%. Most breaks sit in intercompany balances and fixed-asset sub-ledgers. Rehearsal 3 is scheduled for 5–6 December 2026; a fourth rehearsal fits only if go-live moves.
summary: Results of the second ledger migration rehearsal. Reconciliation is improving but still six times the go-live tolerance.

insights.text: Rehearsal 2 left 2.9% of items unreconciled, against a 0.5% go-live tolerance.
Most breaks sit in intercompany balances and fixed-asset sub-ledgers.

title: Pre-implementation audit review
text: Internal Audit rates the ledger partially ready. Control design in the new ledger is adequate, but segregation-of-duties roles for 34 users are not yet mapped. The go/no-go criteria do not cover vendor support or exit arrangements. Internal Audit has not reviewed the CoreSys contract and gives no opinion on vendor continuity.
summary: Internal Audit review before go-live: partially ready, with unmapped user roles and no go/no-go test of vendor support.

insights.text: Segregation-of-duties roles for 34 users are not yet mapped.
The go/no-go criteria do not cover vendor support or exit arrangements.
Internal Audit gives no opinion on vendor continuity.

title: Steering committee · Oct
text: The steering committee reviewed the high rating on R-22 and kept the Q1 FY27 go-live date while rehearsal 3 runs. Decision D-114: a go/no-go recommendation goes to the December board on 16 December, based on the cutover readiness checklist. Procurement was asked to confirm CoreSys support terms before that board. Owners for the intercompany and fixed-asset workstreams remain open.
summary: Records the steering committee keeping the Q1 date despite R-22 and sending the go/no-go decision to the December board (D-114).

insights.text: D-114: a go/no-go recommendation goes to the December board on 16 December.
Procurement was asked to confirm CoreSys support terms before the December board.

title: CoreSys change request CR-07
text: CoreSys has submitted change request CR-07. CoreSys states that standard support for the legacy ledger ends on 31 March 2027 and proposes extended support to 30 September 2027. CR-07 cites clause 14.2 of the CoreSys master services agreement for extension pricing and a 90-day notice period. The agreement is not attached, is not in the vault and has not been reviewed by Legal. CR-07 does not state a price.
summary: Vendor change request to extend legacy ledger support. It rests on a contract clause nobody at Meridian has read.

insights.text: CoreSys states that standard support for the legacy ledger ends on 31 March 2027.
CR-07 cites clause 14.2 of the CoreSys master services agreement; the agreement is not attached and has not been reviewed by Legal.
